pr_title: Change beatmap editor to always select the closest object in time

issue_context.title: When having two objects in the same place, clicking on it should select the object that's the closest to current time, not the first one
issue_context.body:
### Type

Game behaviour

### Bug description

Place two circles in one place, 1/1 beat apart
On the timeline, go between those circles, but closer to the second one (e.g 3/4 beat)
Click on the circle you've placed on the playfield
Notice how you're selecting the first circle (**that's already disappeared**) rather than the one you're seeing. It's insanely frustrating.

Stable has that functionality already

### Screenshots or videos


https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/82095491/95f38066-fb8d-4cbf-9308-fcbdb9ea1c8c



### Version

2023.621.0-lazer

review_comments: It's probably a micro-optimisation, and only probably becomes a relatively relevant issue in https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/24291, but I'm not sure how to feel about `ApplySelectionOrder()` getting called twice with the same argument and then having half the sorted items discarded every time. Maybe better to materialise the collection and use that instead?
I dunno. One would hope this is never going to be iterating over more than 5 or 6 notes (they need to be visible and at the same screen location) so I didn’t over-think it.

I'm _relatively_ sure that `blueprintMap` will have an entry for every single hitobject in the map, not just the alive ones...? Which is why I brought it up to begin with.

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/285a232cc20293f281da6a85e1f69a3d1c9da757/osu.Game/Screens/Edit/Compose/Components/EditorBlueprintContainer.cs#L50
Right. I will change this to use `AliveObjects` or something else.

Actually due to the structure that is really not feasible. If you feel strongly about this, please profile a case you think will be slow. I don't think it's worth worrying about (and I'm not confident materialising an array is going to be much faster, especially since the second usage may never be hit in the LINQ execution as it's only when a cycle happens).

Profiled an extreme case which is basically: take a marathon map, make 2 notes overlap, click on intersection to toggle selection (as stated above requires https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/24291):

https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/20418176/6338e0a4-63ff-4501-a54f-199326b8f372

Results:

| current code | with `.ToArray()` |
| :-: | :-: |
| ![1689872466](https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/20418176/d5be95d2-5ef4-46c3-a129-59cf1765b462) | ![1689872475](https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/20418176/8a59c553-7e87-4733-90b9-de7da1120bcd) |

It's _faster_ with `.ToArray()`, but not sure if fast enough to make worth. I guess we can probably go with the slow version unless this becomes an actual issue? dunno.
Quite marginal. Up to you. I think this could probably be fixed in a better way, if it wasn’t for the edge case of the skin editor, where we’d really want a Drawable.ID for stability..
I'm just gonna go along with this as is to push the series along. If in the worst case the array dump only yields like 0.15ms per call then it's probably not worth pulling hair over..
Should probably have xmldoc as to what this does.
